newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Escondida union calls strike vote Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Chile Escondida union calls strike vote Tuesday.

text.p: Workers at Chile's huge Escondida copper mine will vote Tuesday whether to strike or to accept the company's pay offer in the first collective negotiations at the pit.
Around 350 workers, all union members or supporters, will take part in the ballot which will be held at the mine and in Antofagasta, Pedro Ladra, union scretary, told Reuters.
The union represents a small percentage of Escondida's 2,000 strong workforce.
Ladra said he was confident that the workers would follow union leaders' advice to reject the pay offer.
"The people who vote, will vote to go on strike," he said.
A strike would at 0800 local/1300 GMT Friday, he said.
Escondida, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ plc, is the world's largest copper mine. It produced over 800,000 tonnes of fine copper last year.
